registry_info.name: fractals
registry_info.description: Fractal artifacts - recursion, classic sets, escape-time, IFS, chaos, and useful structures (the /fractal-map chapter).

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Cell edge halves each depth, so a d6 cell is 2.6/64 = 4.1 cm and lands near one pixel at this framing; the silhouette is already converged by d4. Predicted the top pair to twin, and it does - d5==d6 at 2.43%, d4==d5 at 3.65%. The convergence is the sequence's own argument: you pay four times as much and the picture stops changing.

where_the_machine_stops.name: Where the Machine Stops
where_the_machine_stops.description: A Sierpinski tetrahedron at depths one through six - 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096 cells, the count etched on the sill of every frame - and a seventh value, `refused`: the root tetrahedron's six edges in wire and nothing inside, because depth seven is 16,384 cells and the machine declines. The refusal is a VALUE of the axis, not a failure of it, which is the only way a limit gets photographed. Every other fractal gallery here shows the promise of infinity; this one shows it being broken. 2026-08-27.

fractal_antenna_toy.name: Fractal Antenna Toy (hears every band)
fractal_antenna_toy.description: A held Sierpinski-gasket antenna: a self-similar conductor that resonates at many frequencies at once. A fractal hears every band.

fractal_heat_exchanger.name: Fractal Heat Exchanger (all surface)
fractal_heat_exchanger.description: A bench heat-exchanger of recursive branching fins - self-similarity maximises surface area in a finite volume. All surface, no volume.

fractal_truss_tower.name: Fractal Truss Tower (max strength, min material)
fractal_truss_tower.description: A room-scale branching truss whose struts split into thinner struts - the Eiffel trick: span the most with the least.

fractal_antenna.name: Fractal Antenna (multi-band)
fractal_antenna.description: A working multi-band Koch/Sierpinski antenna with a frequency-response readout - the engineering payoff of self-similarity.

fractal_stool_toy.name: Fractal Stool Toy (legs of legs)
fractal_stool_toy.description: A held stool whose leg recursively forks into legs - the branching that holds a tree up holds a seat up too.

furniture_recursion_bench.name: Furniture Recursion Bench (a chair that is chairs)
furniture_recursion_bench.description: A bench showing a chair assembled by recursion: a frame whose corners are smaller frames, down to a real seat.

fractal_furniture_room.name: Fractal Furniture Room (recurse a strut)
fractal_furniture_room.description: A room of fractal furniture - a recursive chair, a recursive table, a branching shelf. Recurse a strut and you get a chair.

fractal_facade_toy.name: Fractal Facade Toy (tracery)
fractal_facade_toy.description: A held Gothic facade panel: an arch filled with smaller arches filled with smaller still. The whole is in the part.

fractal_arch_bench.name: Fractal Arch Bench (span the most)
fractal_arch_bench.description: A recursive arch built of smaller arches - self-similar structure spans the most with the least.

fractal_skyline_room.name: Fractal Skyline Room (self-similar structure)
fractal_skyline_room.description: A room-scale fractal skyline of recursive branching towers and spires - the Eiffel structure at city scale.

recursion_bench.name: Recursion Bench (contains itself)
recursion_bench.description: A bench of recursion: rings within rings within rings, the call happening before each is drawn. A rule that contains itself.

recursive_tree_bench.name: Recursive Tree Bench (two smaller trees)
recursive_tree_bench.description: A bench recursive tree: split, rotate, recurse - a trunk that is two smaller trees, forever, down to the base case.

recursion_animator.name: Recursion Animator (watch the depth)
recursion_animator.description: A device that grows the tree one recursion level deeper each tick, with a depth readout - recursion made watchable.

dimension_bench.name: Dimension Bench (box-counting)
dimension_bench.description: A fractal under a covering grid: count the filled boxes at a scale and read D = log N / log S. The coastline between 1D and 2D.

dimension_room.name: Dimension Room (between 1D and 2D)
dimension_room.description: A room measuring a coastline by box grids at finer and finer scales - the dimension that refuses to be an integer.

dimension_meter.name: Dimension Meter (scan a shape)
dimension_meter.description: A scanner device that measures a shape's fractal dimension - point it at a fractal, read the D.

cantor_bench.name: Cantor Bench (remove the middle third)
cantor_bench.description: The Cantor set on a bench: remove the middle third, recurse, generations stacked - a dust of zero length, uncountably many points.

koch_snowflake_press.name: Koch Snowflake Press (infinite perimeter)
koch_snowflake_press.description: A press stamping out Koch snowflakes - infinite perimeter around a finite area, made on demand.

sierpinski_bench.name: Sierpinski Bench (the same hole)
sierpinski_bench.description: The Sierpinski triangle recursed on a bench - D ~ 1.585, the same hole at every scale, exactly what Rule 90 draws.

sierpinski_stamp.name: Sierpinski Stamp (triangle of triangles)
sierpinski_stamp.description: A stamp device tiling Sierpinski gaskets onto a surface - the triangle of triangles of triangles, as a pattern tool.

menger_toy.name: Menger Toy (held sponge)
menger_toy.description: A held Menger sponge: a cube with its middles removed, recursively. Infinite surface around vanishing volume.
menger_toy.qfep_connection: Depth-3 in the hand: each pass discards seven of twenty-seven cells and recurses on the remainder, so you hold a cube that is mostly its own absence. Infinite surface closing over vanishing volume, at pocket scale.

menger_bench.name: Menger Bench (zero volume)
menger_bench.description: The Menger sponge forming through its iterations on a bench - D ~ 2.73, infinite surface, zero volume.
menger_bench.qfep_connection: The carving shown as a sequence: iterations 0 through 3 sit in a row, volume draining toward zero while surface area climbs without bound. The rule never changes between steps, only its patience.

menger_filter.name: Menger Filter (all surface)
menger_filter.description: A Menger sponge as a 3D filter/scaffold in a housing - the useful side of all-surface, zero-volume.
menger_filter.qfep_connection: Depth by depth the carving trades body for passage until the solid is mostly openings — then a duct housing clamps it and a shaft of fluid pours through, renaming the loss a function. The pathology fractals are famous for, area unbounded and volume gone, is exactly what a filter orders.

mandelbrot_bench.name: Mandelbrot Bench (z -> z^2 + c)
mandelbrot_bench.description: The Mandelbrot set on a bench: z -> z^2 + c asked of every point, the master fractal's infinitely intricate boundary.
mandelbrot_bench.qfep_connection: Each cell of the panel answers a single yes/no — does z² + c stay bounded? — and the black interior is every point whose answer never arrives. The infinitely intricate edge sits at furniture height: the catalogue of all Julia fates, parked on a lab bench.

dna.framing_why: DERIVED FROM THE MEASURED AABB, and the fault it fixes was hidden behind a worse one. Body 1.10 x 1.63 x 0.45 m, diagonal 2.0173, radius 1.0086, projecting 1.157 m wide and 1.834 m TALL at yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26 - a height-dominant subject fitted by its DIAGONAL, so at framing 1.0 the visible frame is 3.83 m and the body fills 30.2% of width and 47.8% of height. verify_batch measured the real subject at 28% x 42% and said so: suspect the framing, not the axis. At 0.55 the camera stands 3.45 m out, the frame is 2.11 m, the body fills 54.9% of width and 87.0% of height, and the scale rises from 198 to 361 px/m - 1.8x more resolution on an escape-time boundary, which is all fine detail. 0.50 reaches 95.7% of height and 0.45 clips at 106%, so 0.55 is the last framing with real margin. THIS WAS ONLY VISIBLE ONCE THE DUPLICATE WAS REMOVED. While the registry declared `figure` twice the sweep compared a frame against itself, the closest pair was a fabricated 0.00%, and no framing advice could be given for an axis that already read as perfectly degenerate. The real closest pair is section vs seed at 0.74%.
dna.still_note: ONE VALUE OF THIS AXIS MOVES AND THE OTHER FOUR DO NOT, so without the fixture the axis is measured against a moving target. _process animates c - c_re = _base_re + 0.12*sin(t*0.35), c_im = 0.6 + 0.08*cos(t*0.3) (julia_bench.gd:227-228) - and the animation is gated at :221 to run ONLY at ladder = figure. Every other value holds c at the export default. The tell is in the sheet itself: the figure tile's own readout says c = -0.35 +0.67i while the other four all say c = -0.40 +0.60i, which is c after roughly 1.2 s of drift, i.e. after the bench's settle. Two captures of `figure` taken at different moments are different pictures, and every pair involving it is confounded - it differs from the others in the PARAMETER as well as in the presentation. THE CURE WAS ALREADY WRITTEN AND NEVER DECLARED. `@export var animate_c: bool = true` exists at :14 and :223 returns early when it is false. Nothing pointed the bench at it, so the shipped default kept breathing through every capture this artifact has ever had. Declaring dna.fixture animate_c=false pins it; the map default is untouched, and the breathing is the point of the artifact in a room - its own sign reads MOVE c, THE SET BREATHES.
dna.measured: MEASURED 2026-08-13, THREE FAULTS DEEP, and each one was hiding the next. (1) The registry declared `figure` TWICE, so the sweep compared a frame against itself and the archived bite report literally carries the row {ladder: figure} vs {ladder: figure} -> 0.0%. The published closest pair was a fabricated 0.00%. Fixed in c00e666f0, and the gate now reports repeated values. (2) With five real frames the closest pair came back 0.74% at section vs seed - and verify_batch immediately said the box was only 28% x 42% of frame: suspect the framing, not the axis. A 1.10 x 1.63 x 0.45 m body is HEIGHT-dominant and was being fitted by its diagonal. framing 0.55 puts it at 54.9% x 87.0% and raises the scale 198 -> 361 px/m. Closest pair 0.74% -> 2.39%, subject 5.1% -> 17.6%. (3) One value of the axis MOVES and the other four do not - see still_note. The cure was already in the code and never declared. dna.fixture animate_c=false pins it, and the sheet proves it took: the figure tile's readout now says c = -0.40 +0.60i like the other four, where it previously said -0.35 +0.67i, i.e. c after the settle. The headline is unchanged at 2.39% because the closest pair is section vs seed, both of which were already pinned - but every pair involving `figure` was confounded before this, differing in the PARAMETER as well as the presentation. 0.00% -> 0.74% -> 2.39%: none of those three numbers was about the axis until the last one.

julia_bench.name: Julia Bench (move c, it breathes)
julia_bench.description: A Julia set on a bench: one c, a whole set; move c and it breathes between connected and dust.
julia_bench.qfep_connection: One complex number holds the whole figure hostage: the bench drifts c by a hair and thousands of multimesh cells reorganise between connected body and scattered dust. Identity as sensitivity — who z becomes depends on a parameter it never chose.

lyapunov_bench.name: Lyapunov Bench (stability landscape)
lyapunov_bench.description: A Lyapunov fractal: colour by how fast nearby paths diverge, and stability itself becomes a fractal landscape.

escape_time_room.name: Escape-Time Room (edge of chaos)
escape_time_room.description: A room of escape-time fractals - Mandelbrot, Julia, Newton on the walls - the edge between staying and escaping.

newton_fractal_tool.name: Newton Fractal Tool (root basins)
newton_fractal_tool.description: A Newton's-method fractal device: z^3-1 basins coloured by which root they fall to - root-finding made visible.
newton_fractal_tool.qfep_connection: Every cell runs the same deterministic descent and lands in one of three certainties, yet the map of which certainty is fractal at the seams — prediction fails precisely where the answers meet. Determinism keeps its promise pointwise and breaks it as a border.

ifs_bench.name: IFS Bench (four maps, a fern)
ifs_bench.description: The chaos game on a bench: four affine maps, a point thrown thousands of times, and a Barnsley fern with no fern ever drawn.

ifs_room.name: IFS Room (a point, folded)
ifs_room.description: A room of IFS attractors - fern, Sierpinski, tree - each a point folded by affine maps, forever.

chaos_game_tool.name: Chaos Game Tool (throw, fold, repeat)
chaos_game_tool.description: A chaos-game device: a die picks a map, a point bounces, and the attractor accumulates out of pure repetition.
chaos_game_tool.qfep_connection: Whatever the spinner shows, the bright point only ever halves its distance to a vertex — and the same Sierpinski gauze condenses out of every reset. The dice choose the itinerary, never the destination: E_flux runs errands for an F_order already written into the three maps.

golden_spiral_bench.name: Golden Spiral Bench (137.5 degrees)
golden_spiral_bench.description: Sunflower seeds packed at the 137.5 degree golden angle - how a plant packs the most seeds, the fractal that grows.

dla_bench.name: DLA Bench (stick where you land)
dla_bench.description: Diffusion-limited aggregation: random walkers stick where they land and grow a coral, a frost - fractal branching from pure chance.

dla_grower.name: DLA Frost Generator
dla_grower.description: A frost/lightning generator: walkers accrete a branching crystal over time - DLA as a growth device.
dla_grower.qfep_connection: Each walker wanders until it touches the crystal, freezes, and is never consulted again — and the tips screen the interior, so the fern's gaps are held open by the same rule that grows its edges. Frost as a record of arrivals wearing the costume of design.

attractor_bench.name: Attractor Bench (chaos with a shape)
attractor_bench.description: A Lorenz attractor on a bench: a deterministic path that never repeats and never escapes - chaos given a fractal shape.

attractor_room.name: Attractor Room (never repeats)
attractor_room.description: A room-scale Lorenz butterfly you walk around - the strange attractor that never repeats and never escapes.

attractor_plotter.name: Lorenz Plotter
attractor_plotter.description: A plotter tracing the Lorenz path with the equations beside it - the butterfly drawn by its own dynamics.

terrain_toy.name: Terrain Toy (held mountain)
terrain_toy.description: A held fractal terrain tile: noise stacked at every scale (fBm) becomes a little mountain in the hand.

terrain_bench.name: Terrain Bench (noise at every scale)
terrain_bench.description: A fractal landscape on a bench: stack noise octave on octave and randomness becomes a mountain, a coastline.

terrain_forge.name: Terrain Forge (stamp a landscape)
terrain_forge.description: A terrain forge that stamps a fresh fBm landscape patch on demand - the fractal as a level-generation tool.

space_filling_bench.name: Space-Filling Bench (a line fills a square)
space_filling_bench.description: A Hilbert curve filling a square on a bench - one dimension reaching, by recursion, to fill two.

space_filling_room.name: Space-Filling Room (every point, one line)
space_filling_room.description: A room-scale 3D Hilbert curve you walk around - a single line that visits every point of a volume.

depth_cap.description: The fractals seam. A Koch curve is infinitely deep; the machine renders to iteration N and stops. Magnify one smallest segment and the endless detail is gone — a straight line. Infinity faked to a budget.
depth_cap.name: Depth Cap
depth_cap.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for fractals. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

the_recursion_cabinet.name: The Recursion Cabinet
the_recursion_cabinet.description: The fractals SUPER OBJECT: a curiosity cabinet built by a function that calls itself - every shelf holds a smaller copy until the base case draws a SOLID block and returns. In the drawers: Cantor's missing thirds, Koch's endless edge, Sierpinski by chaos game, a level-2 Menger sponge, phi's spiral, a Barnsley fern, and escape-time Mandelbrot. Each genuinely recursed. 2026-08-27.
